metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Saudi Arabia

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Saudi Arabia using the OECD PISA 2022 Database tables referenced in the text (e.g., III.B1.2.1, III.B1.2.2, III.B1.2.3, III.B1.4.3, III.B1.4.4). The document does not specify the exact student weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights were used, but PISA results are produced under a complex sampling design with uncertainty intervals (95% confidence intervals) reported for mean estimates. The factsheet also includes comparisons to OECD averages and selected comparison countries/economies, implying that the OECD’s standard weighting and variance estimation procedures were applied in the underlying database tables. No additional preprocessing, ML modeling, or custom weighting choices are described in this factsheet; it is a descriptive reporting note rather than an original student-level analytic study.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive OECD factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking performance and related subgroup/relative-success indicators, rather than an empirical study that models student outcomes with an explicitly stated PV-based dependent variable. As a result, the factsheet does not report a specific plausible-values strategy (e.g., Rubin’s rules) or a missing-data handling method for an ML/analytic pipeline. The underlying OECD database tables used to generate the reported estimates are not accompanied here by the technical details needed to classify PV and missing-data procedures at the factsheet level.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports the analytic sample for Saudi Arabia as 6,928 students in 193 schools who completed the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment in mathematics, reading, or science, representing about 317,500 15-year-olds (estimated 81% of the total population of 15-year-olds). No further inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., specific task completion thresholds, missing-data exclusions) are described in the factsheet; it presents the standard PISA 2022 results for the country.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Saudi Arabia perform on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking test, which measures the ability to generate, evaluate, and improve ideas across three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) and four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Saudi Arabia’s mean creative thinking score is 23 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average of 33. The factsheet reports that 46% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline proficiency), while 9% are top performers at Levels 5–6. It also highlights within-country gaps: socio-economic differences (7.7 score points between top and bottom quartiles) and a gender gap favoring girls (5.7 points). Finally, it reports relative strengths in evaluating and improving ideas and in social/scientific problem-solving contexts, while noting that some comparison estimates require caution due to PISA sampling standards not being met for certain starred countries.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD descriptive results factsheet rather than an original empirical ML paper. It does not specify an analytic modeling pipeline, target variables for prediction, or ML algorithms, and it does not provide the technical PV/missing-data handling details needed for method replication at the factsheet level. Therefore, main_findings and confounders_identified are intentionally left empty because the document reports standardized PISA outputs from OECD database tables rather than estimating models in the text.
